001 · About

FourSeventyEight is face data translated into a typeface, customized by people themselves and built on Archivo Black (OFL).

The name is the number of points MediaPipe's Face Landmarker finds on a face. Each of those 478 points controls a line on the letter. Your resting face sets the lines, and every expression moves them again.

It began as Reflect, a set of mirror slats on Archivo Black, and turned from reflection to the face in front of the mirror. No two people get the same letters. Mouth, smile, brows and gaze each move their own lines, and the left and right halves of a face shape the letter separately.

The family has seven named styles and six axes: mouth open, smile, brow lift, look, left half and right half.

Sections on this page are numbered by MediaPipe landmark: 001 is the tip of the nose, 010 the top of the forehead, 152 the chin, 468 the centre of an iris, 477 the last point of all.

Every letter on this page is cut from Tarini's own face.

234 · Processfacial data to typeface
  1. FaceThe camera finds a face. A relaxed, straight look becomes the resting face.
  2. MediaPipeThe Face Landmarker reads 478 points on that face, every frame.
  3. Mesh faceThe points are centred, levelled and scaled, so only the shape of the face is left.
  4. LineEach point steers a line on the outline of every letter. Expressions push the lines further.
  5. TypefaceThe resting face and five recorded expressions are saved as one variable font.
152 · Built on Archivo BlackSIL Open Font License 1.1
  • Very heavy
  • Neutral
  • Open source
  • Plain grotesque

A heavy, plain grotesque gives every line a long outline to start from, and stays out of the way so the face does the talking. Being open source means anyone's face can be turned into a font they are free to use.

061 · Facial composition and randomtwo ways to wire a face to a letter

Facial composition

The face keeps its own layout on every letter. Brows and forehead move the top of the letter, the mouth and jaw move the bottom, and each half of the face moves its own side.

Random

The face is split into 18 small regions, such as a brow, an eye corner or part of the jaw. Each letter gets them in its own order, so raising one eyebrow moves a different part of every letter.

How A is wired: each letter lays the 18 face regions around itself in its own order, from the top, clockwise. Region 1 drives the lines at the top of the letter. Shown on a reference face; your own font was wired from your face, so its regions differ slightly.
